ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 9.9 km actual against 8.3 km recommended, a deviation of 1.60 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The trip is therefore outside the 'within tolerance' rows of the refund matrix and the deviation is a live one that has to be answered on the facts.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation. The chat log holds exactly two messages, both about the pickup point ('waiting at the library drop-off' and 'thanks coming'), and both sent before the trip started at 18:22:37; the deviation was only detected at 18:27:35 and no message about a route change appears after it. The trip record's own messages_during_trip block, computed under POL-RD-21, is empty, and the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, so no verbal notice can be established on this record and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring one.

The driver's own filing concedes the point: he says the passenger was sleeping in the back and he 'did not want to wake him', which is an admission that no notice of the reroute was given. The rider's statement is that he was awake on his phone and was never told. Either way there is no recorded acknowledgment by the rider, so POL-RD-21's 'agreed deviation' limb is not reached, and row (a) of POL-RD-24 - the only row that returns no money to the rider - is not open on this record.

The traffic justification is not made out. The advisory EV-ADVIS-05016-01 is of an admissible congestion type and overlaps the trip window, but the record leaves undetermined whether it lies on the recommended route: its derived block reports intersects_route and justifies_reroute as null, with the express note that the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 requires a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route, and the driver's assertion of a jam 'after Bukit Timah' does not supply the missing link. On this record the reroute is not traffic-justified, which places the case in row (d) of POL-RD-24.

Even taking the driver's traffic case at its highest, the outcome for the rider is the same. The deviation is over 1 km and the rider was not informed, so POL-RD-24 selects row (b), which likewise requires the excess distance fare to be refunded to the rider. There is no available row that leaves the rider carrying that sum: row (a) needs an informed, agreeing rider, and the chat log and the empty messages_during_trip block exclude that.

The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD = 1.68 SGD. That is exactly the sum the fare breakdown records as already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.68, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED), following the fare_adjusted event at 2026-09-08T00:23:37. The rider is already carrying no part of the contested 1.68 SGD, so the driver's claim for it back is not supported and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03.

The driver's 'I saved him time' is no answer under the matrix, and the record does not bear it out: the platform's optimal duration for the recommended route is 17.6 minutes while the trip took 21.0 minutes, and the recorded distance is 1.60 km longer. POL-RD-24 provides exactly one row and none of them rewards a longer, unannounced route; a route the rider was never told about cannot be charged to him on the strength of the driver's own estimate.

If the judge were to find the traffic question cannot be settled on this record, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human reviewer rather than resolving it against the rider, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held, not collected. So on that path too the rider does not end up paying the 1.68 SGD: whether the case is decided on the matrix (rows (b) or (d), both a refund of the excess distance fare) or escalated (amount held), the driver's claim for the money back fails and the rider keeps the refund he has already received.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory — one of the congestion types that clause admits — on the Central Expressway, towards SLE, at its stated location of after the Bukit Timah Road exit to Braddell Road, and it is valid from 17:57:37 to 19:12:37 on 2026-09-07, which covers the whole trip (started 18:22:37, deviation detected 18:27:35, ended 18:43:37). The CTE and Braddell Road are both on this trip's own route list (Victoria Street, Central Expressway (CTE), Braddell Road, Upper Thomson Road), and the record's own deviation event places this vehicle at the CTE / Bukit Timah Road exit, so the advisory's road, direction and location put it on the recommended route at the trip time. The artifact marks its intersects_route and justifies_reroute values as undetermined and leaves the intersection to the judge; on the road, direction and location that the artifact itself reports, it intersects.

The driver did what POL-RD-21 permits — rerouted in response to real-time congestion — and did it as a single continuous substitution, which the trace shows street by street: CTE until the Bukit Timah Road exit at 18:27:37, Bukit Timah Road to 18:33:37, Lornie Road from 18:34:07, Upper Thomson Road from 18:41:07, ending at the booked Thomson Plaza. That matches the trip record's own route_deviation_detected (18:27:35) and route_rejoined (18:40:38) events: one thirteen-minute excursion, no second departure, no side journey, same origin and same destination. On POL-RD-22's measure — the platform's recorded distances, not the trace — the deviation is 9.9 km less 8.3 km, 1.60 km, the length of one alternative road rather than a detour for the driver's own purposes.

Whatever is owed on this trip is capped by POL-RD-24 at the excess distance fare: 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.68 SGD, computed without surge. Nothing in the rider's base fare (4.50), time fare (6.30), surge amount (4.24) or platform fee (0.90) is refundable; he was carried the whole 9.9 km in 21 minutes to the destination he booked. The ledger shows exactly 1.68 refunded (refund_issued_sgd 1.68, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED), so 1.68 is the entire sum in issue and the driver cannot be charged more than that on any view of the case.

Whether the driver notified the rider cannot be settled on this record, and POL-RD-21 itself treats that fact as unestablishable where there is no recording: the clause's own note records that these records carry no call recordings at all, so the verbal mode of notice the clause admits can never be shown here, and the chat log is silent on the route (trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty; in_app_calls is empty). POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' among the facts whose unestablishability sends the case to a human reviewer, and it forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence; the rider's statement that nothing was said is a party account, not the recording POL-RD-21 requires. On this gap the case should be escalated, not decided against the driver.

If the judge decides this case rather than escalating it, the 1.68 must go back to the driver. The sum was not only refunded to the rider, it was taken out of the driver's earnings ('SGD 1.68 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review', 2026-09-08T00:23:37), and it was taken for a reroute POL-RD-21 permits on congestion that POL-RD-23's own traffic data shows; the sole condition that could make the refund due — that the rider was not informed — is not established on this record. POL-GEN-03 provides the instrument for money the driver is owed, and on this record that money is 1.68.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the platform refunded 1.68 SGD to the rider and took it out of the driver's earnings after the rider's route complaint. The driver asks for it back. That claim fails, and the refund stands.

The distance. The trip ran 9.9 km against the 8.3 km recommended route (EV-TRIP-05016), a deviation of 1.60 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. No one disputes this figure.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA record (EV-ADVIS-05016-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the CTE towards SLE, at "after Bukit Timah Road exit to Braddell Road," valid 17:57-19:12 on 7 September — its window covers the whole trip, and its road, direction and location are on the recommended route's own CTE/Braddell Road stretch. On those facts it intersects the recommended route, so the reroute was traffic-justified. The driver's claim on this point is accepted; the rider's claim that the advisory cannot be placed on the route is not.

Notice to the rider (POL-RD-21). The record shows the rider was never told. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05016) holds exactly two messages, both about the pickup and both sent before the trip began at 18:22:37; the trip record's messages_during_trip block is empty; there are no in-app calls and no call recording; and the driver's own filing says he did not want to wake the passenger. POL-RD-21 puts the burden on the driver to show the rider was informed (in-app chat or a recording), and nothing does. The driver's plea to escalate is rejected: the chat log is complete and unimpaired, so the notice question is answerable — no notice was given — and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. Nor is any other needed fact unestablishable: the deviation comes from the trip record, the traffic justification from the LTA record.

The amount (POL-RD-24). With an over-1 km deviation, traffic-justified and the rider not informed, row (b) applies: the excess distance fare is refunded. It is 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.68 SGD, computed without surge — exactly what the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-05016, refund_issued_sgd 1.68, per_km_rate_sgd 1.05, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) records as already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver. The rider's point that even an unjustified reroute lands in row (d), which refunds the same 1.68 SGD, is right: the outcome for the rider does not change.

Outcome. Because the driver filed to contest a refund the rider is owed, the driver's claim fails and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03: NO_ACTION, with no amount on either side. The rider keeps the 1.68 SGD; the driver's earnings deduction stands. Nothing here generates a referral. The contested value of 1.68 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD AI-final threshold of POL-GEN-22, and the confidence of 0.88 is above the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires, so the AI decides this case.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
